hunks.baseline: But there’s always at least one thing in the world that no one can get used to, no matter how many times they experience it.
hunks.sol: But everyone has at least one thing they can never get used to, no matter how many times they experience it.

hunks.baseline: For me, one such thing was being responsible for other people’s lives. Another was waking up to someone’s ugly face.
hunks.sol: For me, one was being responsible for other people’s lives. Another was waking up to someone’s ugly face.

hunks.baseline: Hyuk Mujin answered, “I was checking on you, Captain.”
hunks.sol: Hyuk Mujin answered, “Checking on you, Captain.”

hunks.baseline: That was a lie. I’d thought half a day had passed at most. I couldn’t believe it had been two whole days.
hunks.sol: That was a lie. I’d thought half a day had passed at most. Two whole days?

hunks.baseline: I looked toward the window, where sunlight streamed in, then sighed inwardly.
hunks.sol: I looked toward the sunlit window and sighed inwardly.

hunks.baseline: “……At this point, it’d be better if I just disappeared. Keep this up and I might get fed up and head back to the Jin Family on my own.”
hunks.sol: “…At this point, I’d be better off not being here at all. Keep this up and I might get fed up and head back to our family on my own.”

hunks.baseline: I had just uncrossed my legs and was about to get up when I stared at Hyuk Mujin, who was putting on a show of threatening me.
hunks.sol: I had just uncrossed my legs and was about to get up. Instead, I stared at Hyuk Mujin and his halfhearted attempt to threaten me.

hunks.baseline: He was talking tough, but his eyes kept darting nervously. A laugh escaped me.
hunks.sol: Despite his words, he was watching me nervously. A laugh escaped me.

hunks.baseline: Hyuk Mujin had been shrinking into himself, either to dodge the punch he never knew when I might throw, or to make sure it hurt as little as possible. Now he looked confused.
hunks.sol: Hyuk Mujin had been hunching his shoulders, ready to dodge a punch that might come at any moment—or at least make it hurt less. Now he looked baffled.

hunks.baseline: “I mean, you’d normally have hit me at least twelve times by now, but you’re just smiling like some virtuous gentleman.”
hunks.sol: “You’d normally have hit me at least twelve times by now, but you’re just smiling like some virtuous gentleman.”

hunks.baseline: I barely held back the laugh bubbling up inside me.
hunks.sol: I barely held back another laugh.

hunks.baseline: Then, in the next instant, I kicked off the floor and shot forward at lightning speed.
hunks.sol: Then I kicked off the floor and shot forward like a flash of light.

hunks.baseline: Hyuk Mujin instinctively tried to defend himself. The movement he showed in that split second was so quick and composed, it was hard to believe he was still only a First Rate martial artist.
hunks.sol: Hyuk Mujin instinctively tried to defend himself. In that split second, he moved with a speed and composure that made it hard to believe he was still only a First Rate martial artist.

hunks.baseline: Of course, the fact that he was facing me meant his response had already failed.
hunks.sol: Of course, against me, his defense had failed before it began.

hunks.baseline: Realizing everything had gone wrong, Hyuk Mujin let out a strangled breath and squeezed his eyes shut. He was probably bracing for the usual bone-rattling blow.
hunks.sol: Realizing it was hopeless, Hyuk Mujin let out a strangled breath and squeezed his eyes shut. He was probably bracing for the hard blow that usually followed.

hunks.baseline: But despite all that mental preparation, what he expected never happened.
hunks.sol: But for all his preparation, it never came.

hunks.baseline: Instead of smacking him like I usually did, I lightly tapped the back of his head and clicked my tongue.
hunks.sol: Instead of smacking him as I usually did, I lightly tapped the back of his head and clicked my tongue.

hunks.baseline: “You’ve been learning martial arts wrong all this time. Who told you to close your eyes?”
hunks.sol: “You little shit, have you been learning martial arts for nothing? Who told you to close your eyes?”
“…Huh?”

hunks.baseline: “Even if you’re getting hit, keep your eyes wide open. Even just keeping your eyes on your opponent puts you halfway there.”
hunks.sol: “Even if you’re about to get hit, keep your eyes wide open. Use them properly and you’re halfway there.”

hunks.baseline: “Isn’t it strange? Normally…”
hunks.sol: “It’s strange. Normally…”

hunks.baseline: “So, you want me to hit you like I usually do?”
hunks.sol: “So you want me to hit you like I usually do?”

hunks.baseline: Hyuk Mujin answered at once. “No. Not really.”
hunks.sol: Hyuk Mujin answered at once. “No. Not that.”

hunks.baseline: “Then shut up. I’m saving your strength.”
hunks.sol: “Then shut up. I’m keeping you fit to fight.”

hunks.baseline: “Saving my strength?”
hunks.sol: “Fit to fight?”

hunks.baseline: “Yeah. We’re going to be fighting like hell soon. Why would I hit you on the back of the head? If you get hit by some stray blade after that, I’ll have nightmares for nothing.”
hunks.sol: “Yeah. We’ll be fighting like hell soon. What good would hitting you on the back of the head do? If you caught a stray blade because of it, I’d end up having bad dreams for nothing.”

hunks.baseline: “I know all about it. When I said I might leave, it bothered you, didn’t it, Captain? Right?”
hunks.sol: “I know. When I said I might leave, it bothered you, didn’t it, Captain? Right?”

hunks.baseline: I was about to say something, but all that came out was a quiet laugh.
hunks.sol: I started to answer, then just let out a quiet laugh.

hunks.baseline: “I knew it. I thought so. Even you need someone like me, your right-hand man, stuck to your side if you want to get anything done.”
hunks.sol: “I knew it. Even you need a right-hand man like me stuck to your side if you want to get anything done.”

hunks.baseline: “Now, why would you say that? Calling me your right-hand man is already a pretty big concession on my part.”
hunks.sol: “Come on, now. Calling myself your right-hand man is already a big concession on my part.”

hunks.baseline: “Yes. Where else are you going to find a subordinate as loyal as me? At this point, I’m not your right hand—I’m your heart. Your heart.”
hunks.sol: “Yes. Where else are you going to find a subordinate as loyal as me? I’m not your right hand—I’m your heart. Your heart.”

hunks.baseline: “Not a chance. You’ve got balls, for crying out loud. How dare you?”
hunks.sol: “Not a chance. You’ve got balls. How dare you call yourself my heart?”

hunks.baseline: This time I put a bit of force into it, but for some reason, Hyuk Mujin clutched the back of his head with a groan, looking happier than ever.
hunks.sol: This time I put some force into it. For some reason, Hyuk Mujin groaned and clutched the back of his head, but his face lit up.
“…Huh?”

hunks.baseline: As I began to question Hyuk Mujin’s tastes, he grinned and went on.
hunks.sol: Just as I began to question Hyuk Mujin’s tastes, he grinned and went on.

hunks.baseline: “It’s just… nothing special. You’ve been acting so different from usual that it was bothering me.”
hunks.sol: “It’s nothing, really. You’ve been so different from usual that I couldn’t help worrying.”

hunks.baseline: “I know you’ve had a lot on your mind lately, but it’ll all work out. So just keep doing what you’ve always done. Same as always.”
hunks.sol: “I know you’ve had a lot on your mind lately, but it’ll all work out. So do what you always do. Just like you always have.”

hunks.baseline: At the same time, the truth I’d kept buried in my heart welled up and tickled the back of my throat.
hunks.sol: The truth I’d kept buried welled up, tickling the back of my throat.

hunks.baseline: I couldn’t let myself speak while swept up in a passing emotion. To survive and win in this enormous gamble, crawling with monsters, I had to keep my words to myself.
hunks.sol: I couldn’t let a passing rush of emotion make me speak. To survive and win this enormous gamble, surrounded by monsters, I had to choose my words carefully.

hunks.baseline: In the end, after thinking it over, I managed to say only one thing.
hunks.sol: In the end, after thinking it over, I managed only one question.

hunks.baseline: “Hm? Scared of what?”
hunks.sol: “Hm? Of what?”

hunks.baseline: “This situation we’re in. And the unknown situation we’re about to face.”
hunks.sol: “The situation we’re in. And whatever it is we’re about to face.”

hunks.baseline: Hyuk Mujin blinked for a long while after hearing me, then answered, “What kind of question is that? Of course I’m scared.”
hunks.sol: Hyuk Mujin blinked at me for a long while, then answered, “What kind of question is that? Of course I’m scared.”

hunks.baseline: “Your words and actions don’t seem to match.”
hunks.sol: “You don’t act like it.”

hunks.baseline: “When I was little, I was afraid my parents’ love would go to my younger sibling, so I cried every day. Then, when I got a bit older and decided to become a martial artist, I’d tremble just from holding a sword. I thought I’d gotten better after joining the Jin Family of Taiyuan, but after I started going around with you, Captain… I really thought I’d piss myself every single day.”
hunks.sol: “When I was little, I was afraid my younger sibling would take all my parents’ love, so I cried every day. Then, when I got older and decided to become a martial artist, just holding a sword made me tremble. I thought I’d gotten better after joining the Jin Family of Taiyuan, but once I started following you around, Captain… I felt like I was going to piss myself every single day.”

hunks.baseline: Thinking back, I’d never really asked Hyuk Mujin much about his past.
hunks.sol: Thinking back, I’d never really asked Hyuk Mujin about his past.

hunks.baseline: I’d only found out by chance that he was the eldest son of a huge textile shop that had been in his family for three generations. It wasn’t as if I’d gone out of my way to learn about him.
hunks.sol: I’d learned by chance that he was the eldest son of a large textile shop that had been in his family for three generations. It wasn’t as if I’d tried to find out.

hunks.baseline: Maybe that was why.
Normally, I would’ve cut off this long-winded story with a flick to his forehead. But today, for some reason, I wanted to hear more.
hunks.sol: Maybe that was why, instead of cutting off his long-winded story with a flick to the forehead as I normally would have, I found myself wanting to hear more.

hunks.baseline: “……Anyway, I wound up stuck to your side somehow.”
hunks.sol: “…Anyway, somehow I wound up stuck to your side.”

hunks.baseline: Hyuk Mujin finished with a shrug, then suddenly looked at me.
hunks.sol: Hyuk Mujin finished with a shrug, then looked at me.

hunks.baseline: “Yes. You’re like a ghost, always heading straight for places where people die. I got so much practice along the way that now, even when I’m scared, I don’t feel scared anymore. You know what I mean?”
hunks.sol: “Yes. You’re like a ghost, always finding your way to places where people go to die. I got so much practice along the way that now I’m scared, but I’m not. You know what I mean?”

hunks.baseline: “Then, was it hard for you?”
hunks.sol: “So it was hard on you?”

hunks.baseline: “It wasn’t hard. I thought I was going to die. But I never actually did. Or, to be more precise, whenever I thought I was going to die, you saved me.”
hunks.sol: “Hard? I thought I was going to die. But I never actually did. Or, to be precise, whenever I thought I was going to die, you saved me.”

hunks.baseline: I swallowed the words that had been circling in my mouth.
hunks.sol: I swallowed the words.

hunks.baseline: Unaware of what I was thinking, Hyuk Mujin continued speaking as if nothing were wrong.
hunks.sol: Unaware of what I was thinking, Hyuk Mujin went on as if nothing were wrong.

hunks.baseline: “Because you figure I’ll save you again this time?”
hunks.sol: “Because you figure I’ll save you again?”

hunks.baseline: For a moment, Hyuk Mujin looked straight at me and spoke.
hunks.sol: Hyuk Mujin looked me straight in the eye.

hunks.baseline: “Oh, I thought, maybe this time I can be the one to save you, Captain.”
hunks.sol: *Oh. Maybe this time I can be the one to save you, Captain.*

hunks.baseline: “You said it was dangerous. That you and Great Hero Jeok might have to risk your lives. That it was basically a gamble. Then this time, couldn’t even a low-level fighter like me be useful?”
hunks.sol: “You said it was dangerous. That even you and Great Hero Jeok would have to risk your lives. That it was basically a gamble. Then couldn’t even someone as weak as me be useful this time?”

hunks.baseline: Hyuk Mujin added with a bright smile, “I may be a First Rate nobody, still a long way from good, but they say in a tough spot, even a cat’s paw will do. Right?”
hunks.sol: Hyuk Mujin added with a bright smile, “I’m still a First Rate nobody with a long way to go, but they say when you’re in trouble, even a cat’s paw is worth borrowing. Right?”

hunks.baseline: No, I couldn’t.
hunks.sol: I couldn’t.

hunks.baseline: It felt as if an invisible hand had closed around my throat, cutting off my breath.
hunks.sol: It felt as if an invisible hand had closed around my throat, cutting off my breath. If I opened my mouth, I was afraid the truth might slip out before I could stop it.

hunks.baseline: I was afraid that if I opened my mouth, I might accidentally let the truth slip out. I couldn’t manage any answer at all.
So I silently looked at his bright smile, then simply smiled back.
hunks.sol: So I looked at his smiling face in silence, then smiled back.

hunks.baseline: “Do you remember what I told you two days ago?”
hunks.sol: “Remember what I told you two days ago?”

hunks.baseline: Hyuk Mujin’s smile faded as he nodded.
hunks.sol: Hyuk Mujin’s smile faded, and he nodded.

hunks.baseline: “Which part do you mean…?”
hunks.sol: “Which part…?”

hunks.baseline: “Oh, of course I remember. But when did you manage to get in touch with the Murim Alliance, Captain?”
hunks.sol: “Oh, of course. But when did you manage to get in touch with the Murim Alliance, Captain?”

hunks.baseline: “That’s not important, so forget it. I have a mission for you.”
hunks.sol: “That’s not important. I have a mission for you.”

hunks.baseline: “No, the entire Fire Dragon Pavilion.”
hunks.sol: “No, everyone in the Fire Dragon Pavilion.”

hunks.baseline: “The entire pavilion means… you’re coming with us, Captain?”
hunks.sol: “Everyone? Does that mean you’re coming too, Captain?”

hunks.baseline: “Are we meeting the Murim Alliance reinforcements there?”
hunks.sol: “Are we meeting the Murim Alliance reinforcements?”

hunks.baseline: “Yeah. They’ll arrive within half a day at the earliest, and by tomorrow at the latest.”
hunks.sol: “Yeah. They’ll arrive in half a day if they’re quick. Tomorrow at the latest.”

hunks.baseline: Hyuk Mujin nodded as if he understood, then suddenly furrowed his brow.
hunks.sol: Hyuk Mujin nodded as though he understood, then furrowed his brow.

hunks.baseline: “But that’s longer than I expected. Being away at a time like this is a bit… And you’re not in your usual condition, either.”
hunks.sol: “That’s longer than I expected. Leaving you here at a time like this is a bit… You’re not in your usual condition, either.”

hunks.baseline: “I’m not. So, are you worried that a Supreme Peak master who isn’t in his usual condition might keel over, coughing blood, at any moment?”
hunks.sol: “I’m not. So, are you afraid a Supreme Peak master who isn’t in his usual condition will keel over coughing blood at any moment?”

hunks.baseline: “Right, I was a crow-tit worrying about a Heavenly Eagle.”
hunks.sol: “Right. I was a crow-tit worrying about a Heavenly Eagle.”

hunks.baseline: “Usually, it’d be a stork you were worried about, not a Heavenly Eagle.”
hunks.sol: “Usually, it’s a stork the crow-tit worries about.”

hunks.baseline: “With the Blazing Flame Divine Dragon, even a Heavenly Eagle isn’t good enough. Anyway, is that the only mission you’re giving me?”
hunks.sol: “For the Blazing Flame Divine Dragon, even a Heavenly Eagle isn’t enough. Anyway, is that the whole mission?”

hunks.baseline: “Yeah. Right now.”
hunks.sol: “Yeah. Leave now.”

hunks.baseline: I answered and took a neatly folded note from inside my robe, then handed it to him.
hunks.sol: I took a neatly folded note from inside my robe and handed it to him.

hunks.baseline: I’d prepared it two days ago, but until the last moment, I’d wavered over whether to take it out at all.
hunks.sol: I’d prepared it two days ago, but until the last moment, I’d wavered over whether to take it out.

hunks.baseline: “People other than me and my Master should be able to leave the imperial palace without any particular restrictions. Once you’re sure no one’s following you, check the destination written there.”
hunks.sol: “Anyone besides me and my Master should be able to leave the imperial palace without much trouble. Once you’re sure no one’s following you, check the destination written there.”

hunks.baseline: Hyuk Mujin carefully took the paper and tucked it away. Then he clasped his hands in a salute.
hunks.sol: Hyuk Mujin carefully took the note and tucked it away. Then he clasped his hands in a salute.

hunks.baseline: Hyuk Mujin, who’d been looking at me in confusion, gave a playful grin. Then he turned and disappeared.
hunks.sol: Hyuk Mujin looked puzzled, then gave me a playful grin. He turned and disappeared.

hunks.baseline: When his presence had faded completely, I slowly left the room and came face to face with the one person still there.
hunks.sol: Once his presence had faded completely, I slowly left the room and came face to face with the one person still there.

hunks.sol: A slow exhalation. Hong Jin looked at me through the cloudy smoke from his long-stemmed tobacco pipe, then murmured as if to himself, “Martial artist Hyuk seemed pretty busy.”

hunks.baseline: “Martial artist Hyuk seemed pretty busy.”

hunks.sol: “He will be. I gave him a mission.”

hunks.baseline: “It must be an important one, if you sent him off at a time like this.”
hunks.sol: “It must be important, to send him off at a time like this.”

hunks.baseline: The old wooden chair let out a groan. Hong Jin rose with elegant poise and spoke through the faint haze of smoke.
hunks.sol: The old wooden chair groaned. Hong Jin rose with elegant poise and spoke through the haze of smoke.

hunks.baseline: “In a dangerous gamble where no one knows what will happen, you must want to save even one more person.”
hunks.sol: “In a dangerous gamble where no one knows what will happen, you want to save as many people as you can.”
